patterns.reminder: jQuery .html(value) parses its argument as HTML. Only pass first-party, already-sanitised markup; never a fetch response, location (hash, search, pathname), storage or form input. Use .text() for visitor-facing messages and insert fetched article HTML as parsed, sanitised nodes (see the article loader in js/app.js).
$(`...${x}...`) builds HTML from an interpolated string, which is an XSS sink. Create the element with a fixed tag and set dynamic values with .text() / .attr() instead.

location.hash / search / pathname are attacker-controlled. Validate them against an allowlist before they reach a URL, a selector or an HTML sink; the article hash is only safe because netlify/functions/article.mts re-validates the filename.

GITHUB_API_TOKEN and the Supabase settings are server-side only. Read them in netlify/functions/*.mts and never ship them in js/, _includes/, _data/ or built HTML. A Supabase service_role key must never be used by this site.
This looks like a JWT (e.g. a Supabase key) or a GitHub token. Never commit credentials: use Netlify environment variables (process.env) for functions and GitHub secrets for workflows.
Everything in PUBLIC_ENV_VARS is returned to any visitor. Only list values that are public by design (ENV_CLIENT_ID, SITE_RECAPTCHA_KEY); never a token, an API key or a Supabase setting.

article.mts keeps two barriers against path traversal: the anchored filename regex (letters, digits, _ and - only, then _xx.html) and the path.resolve + startsWith(articleDir + path.sep) check. Do not loosen the regex or drop either barrier.

Every Netlify function starts with isTrustedRequest(req) -> redirectTo404(), validates each query parameter with an anchored allowlist regex, and ends with catch -> internalError(context, error). isTrustedRequest is Referer-based, not authentication: a handler that writes data, sends mail or spends quota needs real protection.
Do not send error.message or error.stack back to the client: internalError() logs the error and returns only { error, requestId }.
An outbound URL built from a template string is an SSRF risk. Only interpolate values from process.env or from a fixed allowlist (like routes.cvLangs), never raw request input.
The functions are same-origin only. Do not add CORS headers, and never Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * or a reflected Origin.

Do not widen the CSP: no wildcard source, no http:, no new third-party origin without the feature that needs it, and keep frame-ancestors 'none', base-uri 'self' and form-action 'self'. 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' are existing debt, not something to extend.
The contact form only needs the gmail.send scope. Do not request broader Google scopes (gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, mail.google.com, drive...).
OAuth tokens stay in sessionStorage (tokenAPI) and are cleared after sending. Never persist a token in localStorage.
Email header values built from form input must have CR/LF stripped first (see safeSubject / safeSenderName in sendEmail), and the recipient stays hard-coded.
